title: Triage timeline, handoff, and visualization plan for perf regressions
content:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for reducing the friction between on-call alerting and post-incident regression investigations. Focus areas: clear timeline & handoff protocol, minimal snapshot payload to capture for offline bisects, and a visualization/annotation approach for canary vs prod deltas. The goal is faster root-cause hypothesis iteration and fewer repeated escalations.

Context and motivation:
- We keep seeing intermittent p95/p99 spikes that self-resolve but lead to noisy alerts and thrash.
- On-call needs a small, repeatable set of artifacts to triage quickly; investigation teams need richer snapshots to bisect and visualize deltas.
- Existing dashboards are useful but not standardized for canary compare and timeline annotations; different teammates create ad-hoc graphs which slows handoff.

Quick summary of the flow (TL;DR):
1) Alert fires -> on-call runs fast checklist (3 min) and posts structured handoff message.
2) Alert system captures a 5-minute snapshot bundle (metrics + traces + sample requests + config).
3) If unresolved within escalation window, handoff to regression owner with snapshot link and hypothesis seeds.
4) Regression owner runs automated bisect script (SQL + trace correlation) and populates a shared visualization (canary overlay + annotated timeline).
5) Team captures final root cause and mitigation, closes ticket, and saves visualization for postmortem.

On-call 3-minute checklist (to be run in order):
- Confirm severity and scope: check alert rule, affected routes/models, and ingress region.
- Inspect quick dashboard (prebuilt): p50/p90/p95/p99, request rate, error rate for last 15m.
- Run single quick probe: curl /health and a sample generate request to measure synthetic latency.
- If degraded: capture snapshot (button in console or run snapshot-cli) -> generates bundle id.
- Post structured Slack handoff (template below) with bundle id and escalation link.
- If resolved or false positive: mark incident as low-priority and add short note.

Snapshot bundle (what must be captured):
- Time window: t0 - 2m to t0 + 3m (t0 = alert timestamp).
- Aggregated metrics at 1s resolution: per-route QPS, batching size distribution, CPU/GPU util, GPU memory, KV cache hit/miss rates, host-level load, network I/O.
- Latency histograms and percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) per-instance and aggregated.
- Top 200 slow request IDs (request id, timestamp, route, token_count, input_size, model_variant).
- Traces for top 50 slow requests (span breakdown: tokenization, attention, kernel exec, KV assembly, serialization).
- Snapshot of config: model version, quantization flags, kernel selection, autoscaling policy, routing policy, placement region.
- Canary vs prod flags for requests, if present.
- A 30-s sample of raw input for a few slow requests (sanitized).
- Relevant logs (stderr/statsd) for the window and surrounding minute.

Handoff Slack template (copy/paste):
[INCIDENT] {INC_ID} | {SHORT_DESC}
Owner: @{oncall}
Bundle: {bundle_id}
Time: {t0}
Scope: routes={routes} models={models} regions={regions}
Quick findings: p99 up X ms compared to baseline, batch size skewed to N, KV miss rate Y%
Next steps: bisect run (assigned to @regression-owner) and visualize canary overlay.

Bisect/runbook for regression owner (automated-first philosophy):
1) Fetch snapshot bundle by id.
2) Run automated bisect script (bisect.py) which attempts ordered checks:
   - Compare canary vs prod p99 and p50 across the window.
   - Reconstruct per-token timelines from traces to see where delta accumulates.
   - Run delta-by-dimension queries (see SQLs below).
3) If script suggests a likely dimension (e.g., quantized kernel change), run targeted repros on a test node.
4) Annotate shared visualization with hypothesis notes and provenance.
5) If not solved within 2 hours, escalate to on-call lead for resource allocation.

Key SQL snippets (example pseudo-SQL for our metrics warehouse):
- p99 by model variant:
  SELECT model_variant, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.99) AS p99
  FROM request_metrics
  WHERE ts BETWEEN '{tstart}' AND '{tend}'
  GROUP BY model_variant
  ORDER BY p99 DESC
- batch size distribution by instance:
  SELECT instance_id, bin(batch_size, 1) AS batch_bin, count(*)
  FROM request_metrics
  WHERE ts BETWEEN '{tstart}' AND '{tend}'
  GROUP BY instance_id, batch_bin
- KV cache effect (compare requests with cache_hit true/false):
  SELECT cache_hit, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) p95, count(*)
  FROM request_metrics
  WHERE ts BETWEEN '{tstart}' AND '{tend}'
  GROUP BY cache_hit

Visualization plan (standardized dashboard overlays):
- Base dashboard (15m window) with aligned time axis: request rate, p50/p90/p95/p99, batch size mean, cache hit rate, GPU util.
- Canary overlay layer: plot canary series in dashed color on same axes. Always normalize to per-req latency not per-model if traffic mixes variants.
- Trace waterfall: stack span durations for slow requests, allow side-by-side canary vs prod traces.
- Request scatter: x-axis = request timestamp, y-axis = latency, color = batch_size, shape = cache_hit. Hover shows request id and link to raw trace.
- Annotated timeline bar: allow adding short notes at specific timestamps (e.g., deploy at T, autoscaler event at T+90s).
- Composite delta view: subtract canary from prod p99 as a separate series to highlight magnitude and duration of delta.

Visualization ownership and templates:
- Create/maintain a dashboard template in grafana/dashboards/perf-triage-template.json.
- Regression owner copies template -> fills bundle id and time window -> enables canary overlay.
- Add two custom panels: an 'investigation checklist' panel listing the snapshot id, owner, key hypotheses, and links.

Guidelines for deciding canary vs prod significance:
- If p99 delta > 20% AND absolute increase >= 30ms sustained for >2 minutes -> treat as significant.
- If delta is concentrated in p999 or tail <0.1% traffic: deprioritize unless error rate also climbs or user-facing SLAs are impacted.
- Consider throughput drop or batch-size shift as compounding factors even if latency delta is small.

Example hypothesis seeds (use to jump-start bisect):
- Hypothesis A: new kernel selection produced longer matmul runtime for long sequences -> look at model_variant, kernel, and long-seq sample traces.
- Hypothesis B: autoscaler oscillation caused micro-queueing -> check scaling events and batch distribution at instance boundary.
- Hypothesis C: KV cache eviction policy changed -> compare cache-hit rates and latency for cache_hit=false.

Post-investigation artifacts (what to publish inside ticket):
- Final annotated visualization (png + dashboard link).
- Bundle id used for bisect.
- Short narrative: what changed, how we validated, mitigation (rollout/rollback/patch), next steps.
- Action items: dashboard updates, alert tuning changes, test-case to catch the regression.

Retention and learning loop:
- Save visualization and bundle id in a perf-regressions archive (confluence page + S3).
- Weekly 30-min office hours for regression playbook updates; owners rotate monthly.
- Track alert noise metric: fraction of alerts resolved within 5min without action; goal < 30%.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should snapshot window be extended for cross-region network blips? (pros/cons and cost).
- How to standardize safe sanitization of raw request inputs for bundles.
- Add automatic regression classifier to tag 'likely kernel', 'likely autoscaler', etc., based on historical archives.

Appendix: quick commands and links
- snapshot-cli: snapshot-cli capture --bundle-id {bundle_id} --window "-2m:+3m"
- repro helper: replay-requests --bundle {bundle_id} --filter slow --target staging-node
- bisect script: python tools/bisect.py --bundle {bundle_id} --out report.html
- Dashboard template: confluence.redwood/perf/visualizations -> grafana id 2741

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive; feedback welcome on the thresholds and on the minimal snapshot fields.
- Next step once we converge: wire a console button that packages the bundle automatically and prepopulates the visualization template.
